metadata.retired_reason: Prototype-era endpoint with no counterpart: no cairns table/RPC exists and no surface ships a monthly cairn at all — only the weekly roll was ever built. Retire rather than keep an endpoint for an unbuilt aggregate.

nodes.title: select v_pebbles_full
nodes.description: Retrieve a single pebble with all enrichments.

nodes.title: get_pebble_enrichment
nodes.description: Admin-gated analytics RPC. Over a date range, the share of pebbles that carry a picture, a collection, a thought, a soul or an intensity — how much meaning people actually attach.

nodes.title: get_pebble_volume_series
nodes.description: Admin-gated analytics RPC. Pebbles per day/week/month/year over a date range, with the counts that carry a picture, sit in a collection or use a custom glyph, plus distinct active users. Buckets are gap-filled.

nodes.title: RPC path_pebbles
nodes.description: Retrieve pebbles with filters and pagination.

nodes.title: select profiles
nodes.description: Retrieve the current user profile.

nodes.title: RPC get_public_profile
nodes.description: The anon-granted security-definer projection behind /u/{handle}. Builds an explicit jsonb allowlist (display name, handle, glyph strokes, member-since, ripple and bounce levels, the 28-day grid, counters) and returns null for an unknown handle and for a known handle whose owner has not opted in, so the two are indistinguishable to a caller. Never returns user_id.

nodes.title: get_quality_signals_today
nodes.description: SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql RPC, gated on is_admin(auth.uid()). No arguments. Returns all eight rows from v_analytics_quality_signals_today ordered by indicator_order asc. Backs the Quality signals card on the admin analytics page. Raises insufficient_privilege (42501) for non-admins.

nodes.title: get_retention_cohorts
nodes.description: SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql RPC, gated on is_admin(auth.uid()). No arguments. Returns rows from v_analytics_retention_cohorts_weekly for the last 8 cohorts (most recent signup weeks). Raises insufficient_privilege (42501) for non-admins.

nodes.title: GET /auth/session
nodes.description: Retrieve the current session.

metadata.retired_reason: Prototype leftover: `GET /auth/session` was never implemented, and has no Supabase equivalent — the session is read locally via `supabase.auth.getSession()` / `onAuthStateChange` and refreshed server-side by the Next.js proxy, not over a product-owned HTTP contract.

nodes.title: select souls
nodes.description: Retrieve all souls for the current user.

nodes.title: get_user_averages_series
nodes.description: Admin-gated analytics RPC. Per-user weekly averages over the last N weeks — how much a typical active user records, rather than how much the whole base records.

nodes.title: select v_wallet_summary
nodes.description: PostgREST select on public.v_wallet_summary, filtered to auth.uid() and granted to authenticated. Returns one row: balance (from wallet_balances) plus total_earned (Σ credit delta) and total_spent (-Σ withdraw delta) computed from karma_events. Backs the Wallet page summary card in one round-trip.

nodes.title: GET /cairns/weekly
nodes.description: Generate or retrieve the current weekly cairn.

metadata.retired_reason: Prototype-era endpoint with no counterpart: there is no cairns table, view or RPC anywhere in packages/supabase. The weekly cairn is computed client-side from the pebble list (WeekRollCairn on web, WeekRollCairnCell on iOS, WeekRoll on Android). Re-add a real endpoint only if the aggregation ever moves server-side.

nodes.title: RPC is_admin
nodes.description: The admin gate. Returns whether a user id carries the admin flag on profiles. Called by the back-office layout's requireAdmin() before any admin page renders, and re-used inside every admin `security definer` RPC and in the logs RLS policies as defence in depth.

nodes.title: POST /pebbles/:id/souls
nodes.description: Link one or more souls to a pebble.

metadata.retired_reason: Prototype-era step endpoint with no counterpart: souls are the `soul_ids` key of the create_pebble / update_pebble payload, which rewrites public.pebble_souls inside the RPC transaction. No standalone route exists.

nodes.title: select v_logs_with_counts
nodes.description: The single read the whole reader-facing Lab goes through. Filtered client-side into the four feed sections (announcements; feature+shipped; feature+in_progress; feature+backlog) and used again by id for the announcement detail. Web additionally constrains `platform in ('webapp','all')`; iOS and Android do not filter on platform.

nodes.title: select log_reactions
nodes.description: The caller's own reacted log ids, used to render the filled/unfilled state of every backlog reaction button. Anonymous callers resolve to an empty set rather than an error.

nodes.title: POST /auth/login
nodes.description: Authenticate an existing user.

metadata.retired_reason: Prototype leftover: `POST /auth/login` was never implemented. Sign-in is `supabase.auth.signInWithPassword` / `signInWithOAuth` from `useSupabaseAuth.ts` and its iOS/Android mirrors. See API-auth-callback for the only auth contract this product owns.

nodes.title: POST /auth/logout
nodes.description: End the current user session.

metadata.retired_reason: Prototype leftover: `POST /auth/logout` was never implemented on web. Sign-out is `supabase.auth.signOut()` from `useSupabaseAuth.ts`. (The admin back-office does own `apps/admin/app/auth/signout/route.ts`, but that is the w1-admin unit's surface, not this node.)

nodes.title: RPC preview_connection_invite
nodes.description: Definer RPC granted to anon: projects the inviter's display name and avatar glyph geometry for a token, so the accept page can say who is inviting before an account exists. Never raises — returns {status: valid | expired | not_found}; expired and revoked go fully dark. Cross-user reads stay a narrow projection, never a profiles row.

nodes.title: RPC publish_admin_glyph
nodes.description: is_admin-gated SECURITY DEFINER RPC. Atomically inserts a glyph owned by the admin + an auto-approved submission, publishing a first-party community glyph from an uploaded SVG.

nodes.title: insert log_reactions
nodes.description: Upvote a backlog item. A single-table insert on (log_id, user_id) — deliberately not an RPC. All three surfaces apply it optimistically and revert on failure.

nodes.title: refund_karma
nodes.description: SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql RPC, execution restricted to service_role (revoked from authenticated to avoid a client-callable karma mint). Inserts a positive withdraw-side karma_events row reversing a prior spend; the trigger updates wallet_balances. Returns the new event id.

nodes.title: POST /auth/register
nodes.description: Register a new user account.

metadata.retired_reason: Prototype leftover: no `app/api/**` route ever existed in this repository's history, and the path `POST /auth/register` appears nowhere but the bundle itself. Registration is `supabase.auth.signUp` called from `apps/web/lib/data/useSupabaseAuth.ts` (iOS `SupabaseService`, Android `AuthLogic`) — a third-party GoTrue contract this product does not own. The one auth route it does own is the new API-auth-callback.

nodes.title: RPC reject_glyph
nodes.description: is_admin-gated SECURITY DEFINER RPC. Sets a pending submission to rejected with a required review_note (surfaced to the submitter), stamping reviewed_at/reviewed_by.

nodes.title: RPC remove_connection
nodes.description: Definer RPC that severs a connection the caller belongs to, optionally recording a block from the remover against the removed. Carries the extension marker where M52 seams and M53 pairs will be severed in the same transaction.

nodes.title: RPC set_glyph_listed
nodes.description: Admin-gated. Toggles whether an approved glyph submission is listed in the store, without changing its moderation verdict or its price.

nodes.title: RPC set_glyph_price
nodes.description: is_admin-gated SECURITY DEFINER RPC. Re-prices an approved listing. Existing entitlements' price_paid snapshots are untouched.

nodes.title: RPC set_handle
nodes.description: The sanctioned claim / change / release path for a profile handle. Normalizes to lowercase, enforces the 3-to-30 character shape, rejects reserved handles, and raises the three stable codes the clients map to inline field errors (invalid_handle, handle_taken, handle_reserved). Passing null releases the handle and drops public_profile in the same statement, so a profile can never be public without one.

nodes.title: PATCH /pebbles/:id/intensity
nodes.description: Set intensity and valence on a pebble.

metadata.retired_reason: Prototype-era step endpoint with no counterpart: intensity is the `intensity` key of the create_pebble / update_pebble payload (API-create-pebble, API-update-pebble), never a standalone route. No surface has ever called a PATCH /pebbles/:id/intensity.

nodes.title: spend_karma
nodes.description: SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql RPC (granted to authenticated). Guarded, race-safe karma debit: takes p_amount (positive), p_reason ('purchase'), optional p_ref_id. Locks the caller's wallet_balances row FOR UPDATE to serialize concurrent spends, raises insufficient_karma (P0001) when balance < amount, otherwise inserts a negative withdraw karma_events row — the trigger updates wallet_balances in the same transaction. Returns the new event id.

nodes.title: submit_glyph
nodes.description: security definer RPC that offers a glyph to the community store. Rejects non-owners (`not_owner`, which also covers system glyphs with a null owner) and duplicate offers (`already_submitted`, backed by a partial unique index on pending|approved), then inserts a glyph_submissions row at the default price and returns it as jsonb.

nodes.title: delete log_reactions
nodes.description: Withdraw an upvote. The mirror of the insert, deleting the caller's own (log_id, user_id) row.

nodes.title: RPC update_profile
nodes.description: Update the current user profile.

nodes.title: update souls
nodes.description: Rename an existing soul.

nodes.title: Account deletion anonymizes externally-referenced glyphs to the user_id = null system state
nodes.description: A service-role-only `purge_account` definer RPC deletes every user-owned row in FK order in one transaction and returns per-table counts, while glyphs that are externally referenced (foreign entitlements, foreign souls, pebbles or profiles, domain defaults) are anonymized to `user_id = null` and their submissions delisted, because that state is already readable and usable by everyone, so buyers keep rendering with zero schema surface added. The edge function orchestrates purge, then storage, then the auth row last, because that row is the caller's retry credential. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-29 — Account deletion: anonymize externally-referenced glyphs via the `user_id = null` system state; delete personal ledger rows (#631)".

metadata.consequences: Anonymized glyphs become de-facto commons, accepted. Standing rule: every later milestone appends its new user-owned tables to purge_account AND to the verify harness, which is the regression proof. One accepted race converges on re-run.
metadata.context: Store policy required account deletion, and a naive delete-everything hit three traps: buyers hold entitlements on the seller's glyphs, a restrict FK from souls would hard-fail the delete, and a not-null submitter would block the auth delete.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-29 — Account deletion: anonymize externally-referenced glyphs via the `user_id = null` system state; delete personal ledger rows (#631)

nodes.title: Achievements are a client-called idempotent RPC with permanent badges and karma granted at unlock
nodes.description: Evaluation is one client-callable idempotent definer RPC: a stats CTE counts each family once, a single insert-on-conflict-do-nothing against the unlocks primary key records new unlocks, and a chained CTE emits one karma event per newly unlocked badge that carries a reward. No triggers, no cron, and the pebble-creation RPC is untouched; clients fire after count-changing mutations and on screen open, and the screen-open call is the retroactive grant. Badges are permanent, so count regressions are harmless, and the catalog is a seeded reference table kept in sync by a service-role function. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-30 — Achievements: a client-called idempotent RPC, permanent badges, karma per badge via `grant` at unlock (#664)".

metadata.consequences: Standing rule: any migration or admin RPC that inserts an emotion or a domain re-runs the catalog sync in the same transaction. Reward edits apply to future unlocks only, never retro-pay. Retirement is a flag, never a delete.
metadata.context: Eight badge families span six tables, the repo has no cron or realtime infrastructure, create_pebble's return type is a three-surface wire contract, and web glyph carving is a direct insert with no RPC seam, so every trigger, cron or piggyback design collapses on contact.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-30 — Achievements: a client-called idempotent RPC, permanent badges, karma per badge via `grant` at unlock (#664)

nodes.title: Admin glyph moderation: is_admin definer RPCs, admin-owned first-party glyphs, stroke-only SVG import
nodes.description: All admin glyph mutations go through `is_admin`-gated `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs, plus a read RPC that joins glyph geometry server-side so admins can preview pending submissions without weakening the marketplace SELECT policy. Rejection requires a reason stored on the submission and surfaced to the submitter. First-party uploads are owned by the admin user as normal auto-approved listings rather than system seeds, so they reuse all market plumbing. SVG import is stroke-only over a documented element and command subset; fills are skipped and reported. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-06-30 — Admin glyph moderation: is_admin RPCs, first-party admin-owned glyphs, stroke-only SVG import (#497)".

metadata.consequences: New admin-curated goods reuse this gated-read plus gated-mutations shape. A filled-glyph render mode stays a separate future decision. Arcs and smooth curves are skipped, not approximated.
metadata.context: The widened glyphs SELECT policy does not let an admin read a pending submission's strokes, and the glyph model is stroke-only while most real-world SVGs are fill-based.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-06-30 — Admin glyph moderation: is_admin RPCs, first-party admin-owned glyphs, stroke-only SVG import (#497)

nodes.title: Android CI bakes Supabase config into the debug APK
nodes.description: CI injects the Supabase URL and anon key from repository secrets into the `assembleDebug` environment, and the Gradle `secret()` helper reads an env var of the same name when `secrets.properties` is absent, so the downloadable debug artifact is config-baked and actually authenticates. The milestone design had assumed the maintainer would build locally with a secrets file, which is false: there is no local Android toolchain, so a secretless APK crashed instantly on launch. The anon key is publishable and already ships in the web bundle and the iOS app. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-11 — Android CI bakes Supabase config into the debug APK".

metadata.consequences: The maintainer must add the two repo Actions secrets or the APK stays secretless and fails loud at launch. Forks with no secrets still build green. Release and Play distribution were left out of scope here, and reversed two days later.
metadata.context: The app constructs its auth client at launch and throws on blank keys, so the secretless CI artifact was unusable for the only person who could test it.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-11 — Android CI bakes Supabase config into the debug APK; revises D8/D12 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-android-bootstrap-design.md

nodes.title: Android is native Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, mirroring the iOS architecture
nodes.description: Build the Android app in native Kotlin and Jetpack Compose at `apps/android`, structured as a mirror of `apps/ios`: feature folders, injected service objects, hand-written serializable models, supabase-kt, rive-android, Gradle as the source of truth wrapped in npm for Turbo. The real cross-surface contract is the database, so business logic in Postgres RPCs sits equally under every stack; React Native's reuse advantage is modest, Flutter adds a third language with zero reuse, and Compose is the only option with no abstraction tax on the deep-native work that defines the iOS quality bar. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-10 — Android app: native Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, mirroring the iOS architecture".

metadata.consequences: Android joins the web+iOS lockstep on schema and RPC changes, so "keep sibling RPCs symmetric" now spans three surfaces. Models and query strings are hand-written per surface by design: no codegen bridge without a new decision. React Native and Flutter are settled-rejected.
metadata.context: Pebbles wanted an Android app matching the iOS quality bar, built mostly by AI agents with human review, with no convergence of iOS and Android into one codebase.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-10 — Android app: native Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, mirroring the iOS architecture

nodes.title: Android bundles one Nunito variable-font file, not four static weights
nodes.description: Bundle the single variable-font TTF and declare all four weights as four `Font()` entries in one `FontFamily`, all pointing at the same file with `FontVariation.weight(...)`. Google Fonts no longer publishes static per-weight instances for this family, and this is Android's documented mechanism for multi-weight variable fonts; one file is also a smaller APK footprint. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-11 — Android Nunito: one variable-font file, not four static weights".

metadata.consequences: Do not "fix" this by hunting for missing per-weight files: there is no static source. A future weight is another Font() entry, not another file.
metadata.context: The Android design system needed Nunito at 400/500/600/700, and the plan anticipated fetching static-weight TTFs that turned out not to exist.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-11 — Android Nunito: one variable-font file, not four static weights

nodes.title: Android release builds ship to Play internal testing from CI
nodes.description: A dedicated workflow builds a signed release AAB and publishes it to the Play internal testing track via the Play Publishing API: pushes to main auto-publish, a `deploy-beta` label publishes a branch on demand, and dispatch covers the rest. Internal testing is the least-gated track, so the maintainer's phone always has the latest without the manual download-unzip-upload-reinstall loop. Signing reuses the same env-var-or-secrets chain as the Supabase config, and the whole job is fail-soft: with no secrets it emits an unsigned AAB and skips publish. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-13 — Android release builds ship to Play internal testing from CI".

metadata.consequences: One-time console setup only the maintainer can do, documented in docs/android-play-deploy.md, including seeding the first internal-testing release by hand. versionCode derives from the run number, so never re-run a release run: push a new commit.
metadata.context: The device-update loop was manual and painful, and the Play Console draft had just been Google-validated, unlocking automated distribution the 2026-07-11 entry had explicitly deferred.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-13 — Android release builds ship to Play internal testing from CI

nodes.title: Android internal-testing releases bake the wobble experiment in
nodes.description: The Android wobble flag reads a `WOBBLE_ENABLED` BuildConfig field instead of `DEBUG`: constant true in debug, and in release driven by the secrets chain, set true only by the internal-testing workflow. The two platforms' review loops differ: the iOS maintainer runs debug builds from Xcode, while the Android device loop is exclusively the Play internal-testing release pipeline, so a Debug-only gate made the experiment invisible on the only surface actually used. Every other release build still compiles it to a constant false that R8 strips. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-14 — Android internal-testing releases bake the wobble experiment in (#555)".

metadata.consequences: Promoting an internal-testing artifact to a public track would carry the wobble with it: before any public launch while the experiment is unshipped, flip the flag to false and let CI publish a clean build. iOS keeps its Debug-only gate; the golden-fixture parity contract is unaffected.
metadata.context: The Android port mirrored iOS's "unshippable by construction" Debug-only gate, which meant the maintainer's internal-testing build still showed straight lines.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-14 — Android internal-testing releases bake the wobble experiment in (#555)

nodes.title: The arkaik map is served from the hosted project, and apps/admin stays unlinked
nodes.description: A committed project pointer makes the tooling resolve the hosted graph, so the in-repo bundle is no longer the plane agents read; path-scoped repo links move the right platform with no annotation, and ref-policy promotion maps PR opened to development and merged to live. `apps/admin` is deliberately left unlinked, because arkaik models only web, iOS and Android, so linking admin as "web" would mark the customer-facing web app shipped on an admin-only PR. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-28 — The arkaik map is served from the hosted project, and `apps/admin` stays unlinked (#622)".

metadata.consequences: Adding an admin link later is one POST, but only once admin has a platform of its own: do not add it as a convenience fix. The token lives only in an env var, and the tooling errors hard rather than silently falling back to the stale local bundle.
metadata.context: Wiring the repo to a hosted Arkaik project forced two calls rather than configurations: which data plane agents read, and how a four-app monorepo maps onto a three-platform vocabulary.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-28 — The arkaik map is served from the hosted project, and `apps/admin` stays unlinked (#622)

nodes.title: The back-office is its own Next.js app, not routes inside the consumer PWA
nodes.description: Admin lives at `apps/admin/` as a separate Next.js app rather than a route group inside `apps/web/`. The consumer app is a PWA (service worker, manifest, install prompts) and admin work is the opposite of every PWA assumption: always online, never installed, single trusted user. Splitting also keeps admin-only dependencies out of the consumer bundle and gives a clean subdomain cookie boundary. A hybrid `(admin)` route group was considered and rejected. Source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-26-back-office-app-design.md, section "Architectural decision: separate app".

metadata.consequences: A fourth workspace with its own deployment and port; `packages/supabase` is the shared seam. Because admin is not the customer-facing web app, the arkaik hosted integration later refuses to link it as the `web` platform.
metadata.context: The Lab changelog needed an authoring surface, and M26 was the cheapest moment to decide whether admin lives inside the consumer app or beside it.
metadata.source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-26-back-office-app-design.md § Architectural decision: separate app (shipped in PR #318)

nodes.title: Ban `+` in email addresses across auth surfaces
nodes.description: Strip `+` from email input on every keystroke and paste, reject any submitted address containing `+` with a submit-time guard, and show a localized inline error explaining the restriction. Gmail-alias sub-addressing lets one inbox spawn unlimited accounts, and neither RFC 5322 nor Supabase will enforce this, so the clients are the authority. Silent stripping alone would confuse a user whose typed character vanishes, which is why the inline error is mandatory. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-05-26 — Ban `+` in email addresses across auth surfaces".

metadata.consequences: Every new email input surface needs real-time stripping AND a submit-time guard, because autofill can bypass the binding's normalization. Relaxing the rule is a product decision, not a code change.
metadata.context: Gmail sub-addressing (user+anything@gmail.com) lets one inbox spawn unlimited Pebbles accounts; the server accepts `+`, so it is not the authority on this rule.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-05-26 — Ban `+` in email addresses across auth surfaces

nodes.title: Cold launch plays a splash gated on animation-complete AND auth-resolved
nodes.description: A `SplashView` becomes the root content of `RootView` on every cold launch regardless of auth status, running `supabase.start()` in parallel with its animation; the app only advances to Welcome or the tab bar once both the animation has completed and initialization has finished, which removes the `Color.clear` flash the app used to show while the keychain session was read. Superseded in July by the handcrafted-glyph loader, which replaced the launch presentation and its gate. Source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-01-ios-welcome-splash-design.md, section "Splash strategy".

metadata.consequences: Replaced by the handcrafted-glyph loader (2026-07-17), which drops the Rive asset from the launch flow entirely and gates the transition on a real loader-settle event plus auth and reference-data readiness, with an 8s ceiling.
metadata.context: The app rendered a blank `Color.clear` while the auth session was read, then snapped to Welcome or the tab bar. Issue #357 asked for a polished opening instead.
metadata.source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-01-ios-welcome-splash-design.md § Architecture / Splash strategy (shipped in PR #358)

nodes.title: Connections are one symmetric row, invite and QR only, no search, with blocks from day one
nodes.description: A connection is one ordered row with no status column, because accepting the invite is the mutual consent and the invite table is the pending state; the ordered pair plus insert-on-conflict-do-nothing gives structural idempotency for free, which matters because re-scanning a dinner-table QR is the normal case. Writes go only through definer RPCs returning display projections, never a profiles row. The multi-use invite is a plaintext revocable capability stored for re-display, the preview RPC is granted to anonymous visitors so a sign-up-first invite page can render who invited you, the accept-time block check runs in both directions and surfaces as an expiry so a block is never revealed, and blocks ship on day one. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-30 — Connections: single-row symmetric, invite/QR only, no search; blocks from day one (#658)".

metadata.consequences: Later milestones extend remove_connection at its in-body marker in the same transaction. Block management UI is deferred, so until then an accidental block needs a service-role fix. Purge gains three deletes, two deliberately two-sided: do not simplify them. No push, no realtime.
metadata.context: M49 introduces the schema's first user-to-user primitive on a graph where every user table is scoped to its owner; it gates four later milestones, store guidelines require blocking at launch, and discovery is pre-constrained to invite and QR with symmetric consent.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-30 — Connections: single-row symmetric, invite/QR only, no search; blocks from day one (#658)

nodes.title: Cross-user reads are definer-RPC projections; profiles RLS is never widened
nodes.description: One user reading another's data goes through `security definer` RPC projections that build an explicit jsonb allowlist, never through widened RLS on profiles, glyphs or enrichment tables, and never through new views. The public-profile RPC is the template: definer, stable, pinned search path, explicit revoke then grant to exactly the roles that need it, null for unknown and known-but-private targets alike for enumeration resistance, and engagement recomputed internally rather than un-scoping the owner-scoped views. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-30 — Cross-user reads are definer-RPC projections; `profiles` RLS is never widened (#654)".

metadata.consequences: Later milestones mint their own projections with their own allowlists: do not reuse the public one for authenticated-only surfaces by adding fields, and never return user_id from a public projection.
metadata.context: The public profile is the first read of one user's data by another and by anonymous visitors, on a table carrying columns that must never cross users, right after an audit showed how easily wide grants leak.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-30 — Cross-user reads are definer-RPC projections; `profiles` RLS is never widened (#654)

nodes.title: Drafts live in a separate jsonb table, never a status column on pebbles
nodes.description: Drafts live in their own owner-only `pebble_drafts` table whose `payload` is a partial wire payload with unset keys omitted, identical on all three surfaces, so publishing is a pass-through followed by deleting the row. A status column on `pebbles` collapses on contact with the schema: five not-null semantic columns a draft may lack would have to be relaxed for every real pebble, and every present and future view would need a `status <> 'draft'` filter that silently leaks drafts into ripple, bounce and analytics the day someone forgets it. Local autosave stores the same shape minus media, as insurance only. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-29 — Drafts: a separate jsonb table, never a status column on `pebbles`; local autosave is insurance only (#639)".

metadata.consequences: payload is deliberately unvalidated, so create_pebble stays the single validation authority and hydration sanitizes stale ids. Saving a draft must skip the cancel-time media cleanup. happened_at publishes verbatim. Drafts get their own list surface, never an inline timeline section.
metadata.context: M47 shipped quick capture plus per-surface composer autosave, two features easy to conflate into an offline-sync story that had already been ruled out.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-29 — Drafts: a separate jsonb table, never a status column on `pebbles`; local autosave is insurance only (#639)

nodes.title: Deprecate the glyph shape: drop glyphs.shape_id and the pebble_shapes table
nodes.description: Drop `glyphs.shape_id` and the orphaned `pebble_shapes` table system-wide, and update every dependent RPC, view and client reader. No live data flowed through the column: every surface already wrote null, and pebble outlines render from baked-in engine templates rather than from the table. Removing both eliminates a misleading data model, because a glyph is strokes in a square viewBox scaled into the pebble slot and is shape-agnostic by construction. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-01 — Deprecated the glyph shape: dropped glyphs.shape_id and the pebble_shapes table (#503)".

metadata.consequences: Legacy glyph rows keep their original, sometimes non-square viewBox and render fine because the engine fits by viewBox; geometry was intentionally not normalized. Reintroducing a glyph-to-shape association is out of the question.
metadata.context: The shape_id FK was long deprecated: every surface wrote null, and pebble_shapes had no reader once the FK went away.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-01 — Deprecated the glyph shape: dropped glyphs.shape_id and the pebble_shapes table (#503)

nodes.title: Cross-surface data shapes are tested with foreign payloads, and timestamps are parsed tolerantly
nodes.description: Two standing rules. Any shape shared by more than one client is tested on each surface against real payloads produced by the others, verbatim, including precision variants and explicit nulls, with a committed end-to-end harness as the proof where the shape crosses the database. And timestamps crossing a surface boundary are parsed tolerantly and emitted at the narrowest precision every reader accepts, decoded explicitly from the string form rather than left to whatever date strategy the ambient decoder carries. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-30 — Cross-surface data shapes are tested with foreign payloads, and timestamps are parsed tolerantly (#651)".

metadata.consequences: Same-surface round-trips are structurally incapable of catching a same-surface formatter bug, so the test strategy was the root cause, not the formatter. Anything comparing values that have been through jsonb must compare canonically. New payload keys are added to the harness fixture.
metadata.context: The three clients disagree on sub-second precision, so every web- and Postgres-written draft timestamp silently decoded to nil on iOS and a resumed draft lost the time it was captured at, while every iOS test passed because they encoded with the same formatter they decoded with.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-30 — Cross-surface data shapes are tested with foreign payloads, and timestamps are parsed tolerantly (#651)

nodes.title: Glyph marketplace: use-rights entitlements, per-listing price, atomic buy
nodes.description: Buying a community glyph grants a use-rights entitlement row, not a copy, so the original stays single-source and the creator keeps authorship. Price lives on the listing row and is read server-side by `buy_glyph` so the client cannot set it, and each purchase snapshots `price_paid` to preserve a ledger that survives future re-pricing. `buy_glyph` performs the spend and the entitlement insert in one transaction, idempotent via a unique (user, glyph) constraint, so a concurrent double-buy rolls back the loser's spend too. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-06-30 — Glyph marketplace: use-rights entitlements, per-listing price, atomic buy".

metadata.consequences: New store goods reuse the buy_glyph shape (validate listing → spend_karma → grant, one txn). Entitlements are insertable only via the definer RPC. "Glyph value" stays a derived aggregate, never a stored column.
metadata.context: Community glyphs are the first thing the Pebblestore sells; what a purchase grants, where price lives, and how spend + grant stay consistent all had to be decided at once.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-06-30 — Glyph marketplace: use-rights entitlements, per-listing price, atomic buy

nodes.title: Glyph sales pay the creator via a net-zero karma transfer; attribution transfers ownership
nodes.description: A sale credits the glyph owner the full price as a `glyph_sale` credit inside `buy_glyph`, in the same transaction as the buyer's withdraw, so the transfer is atomic and mints nothing. Attribution rewrites `glyphs.user_id`, making one column serve ownership, gallery visibility, the can't-buy-your-own guard and payouts at once. Delisting is a `listed` flag rather than a status flip, so the approved audit trail and existing entitlements survive while buyability stops; deletion is a separate admin RPC and is not reversible. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-01 — Glyph sales pay the creator via a net-zero karma transfer; attribution transfers ownership (#497)".

metadata.consequences: A new glyph_sale reason on the karma_events CHECK; payout is bounded by delta's smallint. Delisting is reversible, deletion is not. Future royalty models build on glyphs.user_id as the creator.
metadata.context: Curation needs arrived: creators should earn from sales, admins should be able to attribute a first-party glyph to its real creator, delist without deleting, and hard-delete.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-01 — Glyph sales pay the creator via a net-zero karma transfer; attribution transfers ownership (#497)

nodes.title: Glyphs become readable when listed or entitled, and listed glyphs are creator-immutable
nodes.description: The `glyphs` SELECT policy widens to own, system seeds, approved-listed, and own-entitled: the single place community glyph rows become readable, exposing only what is genuinely listed or already bought. UPDATE and DELETE are locked once a glyph has a pending or approved submission or any entitlement, so only an admin may then modify it: a frontend-only guard would be bypassable, and cascade deletes would let a creator wipe buyers' entitlements. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-06-30 — Glyphs become readable when listed/entitled; listed glyphs are creator-immutable (D8)".

metadata.consequences: Do not narrow glyphs_select back to own-only: the market and picker depend on it. The web UI reflects the lock, but RLS is the real enforcement. Admins are exempt so moderation can re-price and edit listed glyphs.
metadata.context: A market means other users must read a creator's glyph rows to render and buy them, and once a glyph is sold, letting the creator edit its strokes would be bait-and-switch.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-06-30 — Glyphs become readable when listed/entitled; listed glyphs are creator-immutable (D8)

nodes.title: The app-open loader is a native handcrafted-glyph animation, gated on a loader-settle event
nodes.description: A native view draws the logo stroke by stroke, boils it, then settles, replacing the Rive splash in the launch flow entirely. Every SVG path is its own independently masked wobble ink so one stroke's reveal cannot expose a neighbour's; the creature draws one line at a time via one animation per stroke; one unified render path serves all phases; the boil is a tick count settling only on a clean frame; and the app transition is gated on the loader's settle event plus real readiness (auth and reference data) with an 8s ceiling, never a timer. No spinner anywhere. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-17 — App-open loader is a native handcrafted-glyph animation, gated on a loader-settle event (#598)".

metadata.consequences: The Rive splash leaves the launch flow (the .riv assets and the cairn's Rive usage stay). Android ports per the porting guide, which supersedes the original iOS design spec where they differ. All animation constants are tunable statics recorded in that guide.
metadata.context: The app opened on a fake loader: a Rive logo held by a hardcoded ~2.5s timer, after which a separate real loader could still appear. Simulator iteration surfaced several non-obvious pitfalls this entry pins down for the Android port.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-17 — App-open loader is a native handcrafted-glyph animation, gated on a loader-settle event (#598); supersedes docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-01-ios-welcome-splash-design.md § Splash strategy

nodes.title: Handle policy: lowercase 3-30 characters, trigger-enforced reserved list, freed on deletion, no history
nodes.description: Handles are stored normalized, 3 to 30 characters of lowercase letters, digits and underscore, starting and ending alphanumeric, enforced by a CHECK; a public profile requires a handle; uniqueness and the claim race are settled by a unique index; and the reserved list lives in its own admin-extensible table bound to direct writes by a trigger, because owner-writable RLS makes RPC-side validation alone bypassable. A released or purged handle is immediately claimable: no history, no redirects, so shared links simply break. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-30 — Handle policy: lowercase 3–30 `[a-z0-9_]`, trigger-enforced reserved list, freed on deletion, no history (#654)".

metadata.consequences: Account purge needs no extension, since deleting the profile row frees the handle. Impersonation risk from recycling is accepted at this scale and mitigated by the reserved list, to be revisited if abuse appears.
metadata.context: The handle is the public URL identity, and its rules have to hold against every write path, including owners writing columns directly through RLS.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-30 — Handle policy: lowercase 3–30 `[a-z0-9_]`, trigger-enforced reserved list, freed on deletion, no history (#654)

nodes.title: Track significant decisions in an append-only in-repo log
nodes.description: Keep an append-only ledger at `docs/decisions/log.md`, one terse entry per significant decision, supersede-don't-edit, with a gated PR-checklist micro-step that is usually a no-op. ADRs previously lived only in GitHub Issues: good for discussion, but not greppable, noisy, and invisible to agents at read time, so settled questions kept being re-litigated. The significance bar is "would a future agent or human waste real time rediscovering or wrongly reversing this?". Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-05-26 — Track significant decisions in an in-repo log".

metadata.consequences: Routine choices and style nits stay out. Issues remain the place for discussion; the log captures the outcome. This log is the source every other decision node in this map was mined from.
metadata.context: Decisions lived in GitHub Issues only: not greppable from the repo, noisy, invisible to agents, and therefore constantly re-litigated.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-05-26 — Track significant decisions in an in-repo log

nodes.title: The iOS karma-earned flash is an in-app pastille, not a Dynamic Island Live Activity
nodes.description: Abandon the ActivityKit Live Activity for the karma flash: it is always an in-app "liquid glass" pastille popping bottom-center, hosted in a pass-through window above the sheets that are up at earn time, with a haptic derived from the ceramic sound's amplitude envelope and a countdown ring draining over its lifetime. iOS does not render a foreground app's own Live Activity in the Dynamic Island, and karma is only ever earned by a foreground in-app action, so the real notch could never show this flash. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-01 — iOS karma-earned flash is an in-app pastille, not a Dynamic Island Live Activity (#505)".

metadata.consequences: No App Group, push or provisioning burden. The Live Activity stack is retained as dead code for a future glyph-purchase notification. The scoped `if #available(iOS 26, *)` glass effect is an approved, documented exception to the iOS-17-APIs-only rule.
metadata.context: On-device testing showed Activity.request succeeding while nothing rendered in the notch, on the Lock Screen, or when backgrounded. The concern had been raised during brainstorming, wrongly walked back, then confirmed by device evidence.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-01 — iOS karma-earned flash is an in-app pastille, not a Dynamic Island Live Activity (#505); revises D3 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-01-issue-505-ios-karma-earned-flash-design.md

nodes.title: iOS is native SwiftUI on iOS 17, iPhone-only, with an XcodeGen-generated project
nodes.description: The iOS app is a native SwiftUI target deploying to iOS 17.0 (modern SwiftUI and `@Observable` with no backports), iPhone-only to mirror the mobile-first web PWA, with the `.xcodeproj` treated as a regeneratable XcodeGen artifact so `project.pbxproj` never conflicts. One Supabase project serves Debug and Release via a git-ignored `Config/Secrets.xcconfig` read through a typed `AppEnvironment`; tests are unit-only under Swift Testing, and linting is SwiftLint. No repository or use-case abstractions were introduced up front. Source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-12-ios-project-bootstrap-design.md, section "Key decisions".

metadata.consequences: XcodeGen regeneration is a required step before any build; the two-tab shell (Path, Profile) fixed the app's information architecture; Swift Testing (never XCTest) and SwiftLint are the surface's standing gates.
metadata.context: First SwiftUI project in the repo. The deliverable was explicitly the project structure and tooling choices, not any feature.
metadata.source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-12-ios-project-bootstrap-design.md § Key decisions (shipped in PR #242)

nodes.title: Karma wallet: one ledger, debt allowed, refunds server-only
nodes.description: Keep a single `karma_events` ledger with a credit/withdraw axis keyed off movement category rather than sign, and a balance snapshot in `wallet_balances`. The non-negative rule lives only in the row-locked `spend_karma` RPC; there is deliberately no `CHECK(balance >= 0)`, so earn-side clawbacks (deleting a pebble) may drive the balance negative as a debt the user clears by re-earning. `refund_karma` is `service_role`-only, because granting it to `authenticated` would be a karma-minting hole. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-06-29 — Karma wallet: one ledger, debt allowed, refunds server-only".

metadata.consequences: Do not add CHECK(balance >= 0) to wallet_balances: it would break pebble deletion. New spend reasons go through spend_karma; new earn reasons just insert credit events. `delta` stays smallint.
metadata.context: Making karma spendable (M36 Pebblestore) meant turning an earn-only ledger into a currency whose balance can go down, without breaking pebble deletion's karma clawback.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-06-29 — Karma wallet: one ledger, debt allowed, refunds server-only

nodes.title: Lab Notes are a strict YAML snippet that prefills the admin from the clipboard
nodes.description: The PR Lab Note becomes a strict YAML snippet matching the `logs` columns, authored via a repo-local skill that carries the schema, allowed values and a friendly bilingual tone. In the admin, clicking "New log" reads the clipboard during the click gesture and, when it holds a matching snippet, opens the existing form prefilled: no import page, no new server action, all existing validation reused. This removes the manual re-keying and fixes the voice at the source. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-17 — Lab Notes are a YAML snippet that prefills the admin from the clipboard (#601)".

metadata.consequences: The parser tolerates both idiomatic YAML and the issue's list-of-dashes style; any clipboard failure falls back to a blank form. The old free-form markdown shape is retired, and dossier harvesting now expects the YAML block.
metadata.context: The Lab Note step produced an ad-hoc bilingual markdown blurb the maintainer had to re-key by hand, and the PR template's "voice anchors" mechanism was clunky with an unsatisfying result.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-17 — Lab Notes are a YAML snippet that prefills the admin from the clipboard (#601)

nodes.title: Local-first data provider: localStorage is the primary store, Supabase syncs in the background
nodes.description: Replace `LocalProvider` with a `SupabaseProvider` that keeps localStorage as the primary store for instant reads and writes, mutating an in-memory store, persisting to localStorage, then firing a background push to Supabase that the UI never waits on. On every mount, local state is loaded first, then Supabase is fetched as the source of truth and replaces it. Superseded the same day by the source-of-truth redesign. Source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-11-supabase-provider-design.md, sections "Overview" and "Architecture".

metadata.consequences: Optimistic writes with fire-and-forget push produced diverging caches, swallowed failures and duplicate pebbles within hours; the redesign of the same day deleted the local cache and the provider switching entirely.
metadata.context: The app was moving off localStorage-only storage and wanted to keep the instant, never-blocking feel of local reads while gaining a real backend.
metadata.source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-11-supabase-provider-design.md (shipped in PR #229, "feat(db): implement local-first SupabaseProvider")

nodes.title: Two migrations re-emitting one function off the same base need a manual union
nodes.description: The in-body append-marker convention is kept but is not collision-safe on its own: when two open branches both re-emit the same whole-body function, the merge is a manual union, re-emitted once more in a new migration carrying both appends. `create or replace function` has no merge semantics, the last writer by timestamp wins the entire body, git reports no conflict because the migrations are different files, and reviewing either PR in isolation cannot catch it. The standing rule now extends to the harness, which is what turns the collision from silent into loud. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-31 — Two migrations re-emitting one function off the same base silently drop each other's appends (#687)".

metadata.consequences: A table added to purge_account gains its seed and its zero-row assertion in the verify harness in the same change, and that harness runs after any batch touching purge_account, not just after a single PR. The next likely collision is already named.
metadata.context: Achievements and mutual connections landed within hours, each re-emitting purge_account with its own append; by timestamp the merged history kept one and silently lost the other's three tables. Both branches were green in isolation.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-31 — Two migrations re-emitting one function off the same base silently drop each other's appends (#687)

nodes.title: Offline is a non-goal on every surface
nodes.description: Offline is explicitly not a goal on web, iOS or Android. Local autosave and the server drafts table do not change that: the local snapshot is crash and offline insurance for the open composer only, with no merge logic, no cross-device sync, and clearing on publish. The web service worker keeps Supabase requests network-only, because a cached-401-after-sign-in bug already proved that caching Supabase responses is unsafe. Recording it stops the question being re-litigated. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-29 — Offline is a non-goal on every surface (#620)".

metadata.consequences: Do not add a Supabase caching strategy to the service worker, or local-first sync logic to autosave and drafts, without first superseding this entry. Composer insurance stays local-only and single-device.
metadata.context: The store-launch parity audit flagged that offline was a non-goal everywhere but recorded nowhere, and the drafts milestone introduced a local snapshot that could be misread as offline capability.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-29 — Offline is a non-goal on every surface (#620)

nodes.title: PostgreSQL-first relational schema with UUID keys and layered migrations
nodes.description: Migrate the data layer from client-side localStorage to a fully relational Supabase schema: normalized tables and join tables (no document-style storage), UUID primary keys everywhere with human-readable identifiers kept as non-FK `slug` columns, `user_id` on every content table so RLS is an `auth.uid()` equality check, Supabase Auth plus an app-owned `profiles` table, and four layered migrations (reference tables, core tables + RLS + indexes, views, RPCs) each independently reviewable. Source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-11-database-schema-design.md, section "Principles".

metadata.consequences: Every later content table inherits the `user_id` + RLS pattern; slugs are display identifiers only and never FK targets; the layer order (tables → views → RPCs) is the shape every subsequent migration batch follows.
metadata.context: Pebbles stored everything in the browser's localStorage. Going multi-surface required a real backend, and the shape of that backend would constrain every client that followed.
metadata.source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-11-database-schema-design.md § Principles / Migration Strategy (shipped in PR #225)

nodes.title: Prefer RPCs for multi-table or multi-statement Supabase writes
nodes.description: Before writing any Supabase query that touches more than one table or does more than a single-row read/write, check the migrations for an existing RPC and call it; if none exists, create one rather than chaining client calls. PostgREST has no client-side transactions, so a client-stitched multi-table write leaves the database inconsistent on partial failure, while an RPC runs in one Postgres transaction and can enforce ownership past `security definer`. Sibling RPCs stay symmetric. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-05-26 — Prefer RPCs for multi-table or multi-statement Supabase writes".

metadata.consequences: Single-table single-statement calls stay direct. Extending an existing RPC beats re-implementing it client-side. This is also what makes the database, not a shared client library, the real cross-surface contract.
metadata.context: Client-stitched multi-table writes are not atomic, and RLS-only ownership checks are hard to keep symmetric across surfaces.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-05-26 — Prefer RPCs for multi-table or multi-statement Supabase writes

nodes.title: Promote learnings into CLAUDE.md only on hardening, via a milestone grooming pass
nodes.description: A learning becomes a CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rule only when it is both durable (outlives the next refactor) and action-guiding (tells a future agent what to do or avoid), and only during the monorepo-audit grooming pass at milestone boundaries. Never a per-PR edit. Cheap capture in plans' "Lessons learned" plus expensive promotion keeps the most token-precious files in the repo small and high-signal while losing nothing. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-05-26 — Promote learnings into CLAUDE.md only on hardening, via a milestone grooming pass".

metadata.consequences: Reviewers can reject CLAUDE.md edits that fail the durable + action-guiding bars; the grooming pass also demotes and deletes rules that went stale.
metadata.context: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md load into every agent context, so per-PR learning edits bloat them and dilute their signal.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-05-26 — Promote learnings into CLAUDE.md only on hardening, via a milestone grooming pass

nodes.title: Deploy to remote Supabase instead of local Docker
nodes.description: Test edge functions, migrations and database changes against the remote Supabase project rather than local containers, using `supabase db push` and `supabase functions deploy`. The Docker-based local workflow fails often enough on the maintainer's machine to block work, while the remote project is reliable and cheap to iterate against at this team size. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-05-26 — Deploy to remote Supabase instead of local Docker".

metadata.consequences: Plans, verification steps and onboarding are written remote-first. Anyone proposing a local-Docker step confirms it works end-to-end on the maintainer's setup first.
metadata.context: The standard local Supabase workflow (supabase start, functions serve, db:reset) depends on Docker, a constant source of friction on the maintainer's machine.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-05-26 — Deploy to remote Supabase instead of local Docker

nodes.title: Petroglyph wobble is generated at runtime on-device, as leaky filled outlines
nodes.description: Wobble is computed at runtime on-device (iOS first, Debug-gated) as a fractalNoise port, flatten, dual-edge outline, displace and fill, rather than baked at build time or written into the stored render. Glyphs are user-carved and marketplace-traded so build-time baking is impossible, and a server-side bake would iterate slowly, grow the stored SVG five to fifteen times, and still miss every glyph-only surface. The approved look is filled outlines whose width breathes, which a stroked centerline cannot reproduce. Cross-platform parity is anchored by regenerable golden fixtures. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-13 — Petroglyph wobble is generated at runtime on-device (iOS-first), as leaky filled outlines (#555)".

metadata.consequences: render_svg and render_version are untouched: do not bump the engine or backfill for wobble. Android and web ports must pass the golden fixtures. Do not "correct" the displacement sign, and do not substitute another noise: both change the approved look.
metadata.context: The source issue recommended baking wobble at build time so every platform ships identical static paths, which collapses against user-carved, traded glyphs and client-side previews that bypass the stored render.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-13 — Petroglyph wobble is generated at runtime on-device (iOS-first), as leaky filled outlines (#555)

nodes.title: Pebble artwork is composed server-side by an edge function wrapping create_pebble
nodes.description: The client-facing `compose-pebble` edge function wraps the existing `create_pebble` RPC rather than porting its PL/pgSQL to Deno, preserving the single-transaction insert; an ops-only, service-role `backfill-pebble-render` shares the same `_shared/compose-and-write.ts` helper so the two paths cannot diverge. Each invocation uses two clients: auth-forwarded for the RPC (so `auth.uid()` resolves for ownership and karma) and admin for writing the server-owned render columns the user must not be able to spoof. `render_version` pins the whole rendering contract. Source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-15-remote-pebble-engine-slice-1-design.md, section "Decisions" (1-4, 13).

metadata.consequences: The RPC becomes an internal implementation detail of the edge function; render columns are server-owned; a pebble whose compose failed renders text-only and heals on the next backfill rather than blocking or crashing the client.
metadata.context: iOS needed to display real pebble artwork without reimplementing the web engine in Swift, and the engine had to stay in exactly one place across surfaces.
metadata.source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-15-remote-pebble-engine-slice-1-design.md § Decisions 1-4 and 13 (shipped in PR #262)

nodes.title: Supabase is the source of truth: no local cache, no provider switching, no anonymous data layer
nodes.description: Mutations go to Supabase first and local state updates only on success; there is no localStorage cache for data, `LocalProvider` is deleted, and `DataProvider` creates a single `SupabaseProvider` when authenticated with no fallback. Offline degrades gracefully to read-only last-loaded data with mutations blocked and a visible message, and the landing page shows static seed content with no provider and no hooks. Source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-11-auth-data-layer-redesign.md, section "Design Decisions" (1-4).

metadata.consequences: One provider, one source of truth; failures surface instead of being swallowed. The `onAuthStateChange` reentrancy rail (never await Supabase inside the callback) comes from the same work and is still a standing rule.
metadata.context: The two-provider architecture had interacting race conditions: session loss on refresh, pebbles never reaching Supabase, duplicated pebbles, blank screens during auth transitions, and no error feedback. The cache diverging from the server was the root cause.
metadata.source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-11-auth-data-layer-redesign.md § Design Decisions (shipped in PR #234, deadlock fix in PR #239)

nodes.title: System glyphs are real rows in glyphs with user_id = NULL
nodes.description: Domain fallback glyphs live as ordinary `public.glyphs` rows with `user_id = NULL`, referenced by `domains.default_glyph_id`, rather than as a separate table or bundled assets. `glyphs.user_id` becomes nullable and the SELECT policy is relaxed so system glyphs are globally readable, while insert/update/delete stay user-scoped. Source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-15-remote-pebble-engine-slice-1-design.md, section "Decisions" (5).

metadata.consequences: `user_id = NULL` becomes the schema's standing "readable and usable by everyone" glyph state, which account deletion later reuses to anonymize glyphs other people paid for instead of revoking them.
metadata.context: Every pebble needs a glyph slot to render, including pebbles whose author never carved one, so a fallback had to exist that any user can read.
metadata.source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-15-remote-pebble-engine-slice-1-design.md § Decisions 5 (shipped in PR #262)

nodes.title: Postgres views are security_invoker by default; auth.uid() filters are not a substitute
nodes.description: Every new or recreated view in `public` is created with `security_invoker = true` and paired with an explicit revoke from public and anon plus a grant to authenticated when it exposes user data. A trailing `auth.uid()` filter only protects views shaped one-row-per-user, cannot scope a view that fans out over per-row child data, and silently disappears if a later create-or-replace drops it; `security_invoker` delegates to base-table RLS, which is already the reviewed source of truth. Default privileges mean "no explicit grant" is not "no access", it is access for anon. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-07-29 — Postgres views are `security_invoker` by default; `auth.uid()` filters are not a substitute (#616)".

metadata.consequences: Reads now depend on base-table RLS, which is safe by construction here. The bolt-on auth.uid() filter is retained where it already works but is not the pattern to copy. Client-side user filters become redundant but stay harmless.
metadata.context: A core view shipped without security_invoker and ran with definer rights, so a probe with only the publishable key and no session returned 182 pebbles across 20 users while the underlying table correctly returned nothing. It was the second occurrence of the class.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-07-29 — Postgres views are `security_invoker` by default; `auth.uid()` filters are not a substitute (#616)

nodes.title: Web in-app activity is Sonner plus explicit fire at the action site, not realtime
nodes.description: Build in-app activity on Sonner, rendering a compact custom pill bottom-center, and trigger it by explicit fire at the action site: the mutation hooks read karma from provider truth before and after the action and call `notifyKarma(delta, reason)` on a positive delta. No Supabase realtime and no central balance-watcher, because realtime would be heavier and would double-fire against the optimistic store reload. Source: docs/decisions/log.md, entry "2026-06-29 — Web in-app notifications: Sonner + explicit-fire, no realtime".

metadata.consequences: New credit sources add one notifyKarma call at their action site, on the hook the live surface actually uses. Credit-only by design: clawbacks stay silent. A stable toast id means a new credit replaces the prior one.
metadata.context: A web PWA cannot render into the iOS Dynamic Island, so the admired Opal effect had to be approximated within web limits, and the app needed a way to know a credit happened.
metadata.source: docs/decisions/log.md § 2026-06-29 — Web in-app notifications: Sonner + explicit-fire, no realtime

nodes.title: Account
nodes.description: User account with username and hashed password credentials.

nodes.title: Achievement
nodes.description: Unlockable reward earned through collecting and engagement.

nodes.title: achievement_unlocks
nodes.description: One row per badge a person has earned, with the instant it was earned. Written only by check_achievements(), which is idempotent, so re-evaluating never double-grants or double-pays karma.

nodes.title: achievements
nodes.description: The badge catalog: slug, family, threshold, sort order, karma reward, an active flag and optional per-locale title/description overrides that win over the client's family-keyed copy. Kept in step with the emotion and domain reference tables by sync_achievement_catalog().

nodes.title: bounces
nodes.description: Postgres table: snapshot of each user's running bounce karma score. Columns: user_id (PK, FK auth.users), score (int, default 0; cumulative sum of karma_events.delta — may be transiently negative if reversals exceed gains, the analytics view floors at 0), updated_at. Maintained atomically by trigger karma_events_apply_to_bounce on every karma_events insert (upserts the delta in the same transaction). Backfilled at migration time from sum(karma_events.delta) per user. RLS: users can read their own row; writes only via the trigger (security definer).

nodes.title: Cairn
nodes.description: Weekly or monthly wrap stacking pebbles into a summary.

nodes.title: Card
nodes.description: Media or content card attached to a pebble.

nodes.title: Collection
nodes.description: A curated group of pebbles with rise progression.

nodes.title: connection_blocks
nodes.description: Directed blocks, PK (blocker_id, blocked_id), recorded when a connection is removed with the block option. Checked by accept in BOTH directions, surfaced as invite_expired so a block is never confirmed to the blocked user. Present from day one for the store UGC requirements; management UI lands with M56.

nodes.title: connection_invites
nodes.description: Invite tokens: inviter_id, a unique 32-byte base64url token, created_at, expires_at (default 7 days) and revoked_at. Multi-use until revoked or expired, with a partial unique index enforcing at most one live invite per user. SELECT-only RLS scoped to the inviter, which is what keeps the plaintext token safe.

nodes.title: connections
nodes.description: Single-row symmetric link between two users: (user_a, user_b) with a user_a < user_b CHECK and a unique pair. No status column — accepting the invite IS the mutual consent, so there is no pending state between two known users. Written only by the definer RPCs; SELECT-only RLS scoped to either member.

nodes.title: Domain
nodes.description: Life domain from the revisited Maslow pyramid.

nodes.title: Emotion Category & Palette
nodes.description: public.emotion_categories table grouping emotions (anger, fear, joy, peace, pride, sadness, shame) with an inlined four-color palette: primary_color, secondary_color, light_color, surface_color (all 8-digit #RRGGBBAA). public.emotions.category_id NOT NULL FK joins to it. The view public.v_emotions_with_palette is an INNER JOIN of emotions and emotion_categories that clients consume to render pebble strokes (primary in light mode, secondary in dark) and the emotion meta pill (primary background, light foreground). Schema shipped in #367; iOS consumer in #369.

nodes.title: Emotion Pearl
nodes.description: Nuanced emotional shape attached to a pebble.

metadata.retired_reason: No `emotion_pearls` table exists in `packages/supabase/supabase/migrations`, and no type, field or string named pearl survives on web, iOS or Android (the only hits are legacy prose in `docs/terms/*.md`). The concept died with the pearl visualizer in #161.

nodes.title: glyph_entitlements
nodes.description: Per-user glyph ownership grants from the marketplace: (user_id, glyph_id, price_paid, created_at). Written by buy_glyph; read by the Owned tab. RLS: caller sees only their own entitlements.

nodes.title: glyph_favourites
nodes.description: Heart-toggle join table (user_id, glyph_id) behind the store's Favourites tab. RLS-scoped to the caller and surfaced as the `favourited` flag on v_glyph_market. Written only by the web store; iOS and Android ship no favourite affordance.

nodes.title: glyph_submissions
nodes.description: A community glyph submission and its market listing (#496). Columns: glyph_id, submitter_id, status (pending/approved/rejected), price, review_note (#497 admin reason), reviewed_at/reviewed_by. At most one active (pending|approved) submission per glyph.

nodes.title: glyphs
nodes.description: User-drawn (or admin-uploaded) glyph marks: stroke-only geometry (strokes JSONB of {d,width} + view_box), optional name, nullable user_id (NULL = system seed). Rendered recolored by emotion. SELECT widened (D8) to own ∪ seeds ∪ approved-listed ∪ entitled; UPDATE/DELETE locked once listed/bought (admin-exempt).

nodes.title: Instant
nodes.description: A compressed photo attached to a pebble, stored as a base64 JPEG data URI.

nodes.title: karma_events
nodes.description: Postgres append-only karma ledger. Each row carries a smallint delta plus a type axis (credit = earn-side: pebble_created/pebble_enriched/pebble_deleted/grant; withdraw = spend-side: purchase/refund), making karma a spendable currency. balance = Σ delta; earned = Σ delta where credit; spent = -Σ delta where withdraw. Inserts fire two triggers: apply_karma_event_to_wallet (all events) and apply_karma_event_to_bounce (credit-only, so the bounce snapshot stays earned-karma). Indexed on (user_id, type) and (user_id, created_at desc).

nodes.title: log_reactions
nodes.description: Backlog upvotes, PK (log_id, user_id). Written by direct single-table insert/delete from every client — the sanctioned no-RPC pattern; clients toggle optimistically and revert both the reacted set and the count on error (no refetch).

nodes.title: logs
nodes.description: The Lab log table: one changelog entry or announcement, bilingual (title/summary/body in EN and FR), with species, platform, status, published flag, release date and cover image. The back-office reads and writes it directly over PostgREST; RLS requires is_admin() for any write or unpublished read.

nodes.title: Mark
nodes.description: A glyph rendered into a pebble slot (shape-agnostic square), stored as SVG strokes. The is_custom flag (generated from user_id IS NOT NULL) distinguishes user-drawn glyphs from per-domain system seeds, and powers the % custom-glyph creativity signal in admin analytics.

nodes.title: Pebble
nodes.description: A single recorded memory with intensity, 3-level positiveness, a privacy grade (secret to just you, private to your connections, public to anyone), and timestamp.

nodes.title: pebble_drafts
nodes.description: Unpublished pebble drafts: owner-scoped rows holding a PARTIAL compose-pebble wire payload as jsonb, with created_at/updated_at (trigger-maintained, the list orders on it). Deliberately a separate table rather than a status column on pebbles — five NOT NULL semantic columns a draft may all lack, and create_pebble is the schema's only karma emitter, so keeping drafts off it makes zero karma structural (M47 design D1). Payload is intentionally unvalidated; create_pebble stays the validation authority at publish time.

nodes.title: Pebble Engine
nodes.description: Pure TypeScript rendering engine that generates SVG pebble visuals from pebble data; designed for extraction as @pebbles/engine.

nodes.title: Profile
nodes.description: User profile with display name, onboarding state, color world preference, and consent timestamps (terms_accepted_at, privacy_accepted_at).

nodes.title: reserved_handles
nodes.description: Handles nobody can claim — brand, system and route-colliding words. Enforced by a trigger as well as by set_handle, so a direct client write cannot slip one past.

nodes.title: Soul
nodes.description: A person linked to pebbles, representing someone in the user's life. Each soul carries a glyph for visual identity.

nodes.title: Thought
nodes.description: Scoped written reflection tied to a pebble.

metadata.retired_reason: Thought was never a stored entity — it survives only as the `thoughts` slug of a card type in `lib/config/card-types.ts`. There is no `thoughts` table, no `thoughts` field on any Pebble type, and no client surface. Retired as a prototype-era concept node.

nodes.title: v_analytics_active_users_daily
nodes.description: Postgres view: projection of v_analytics_kpi_daily exposing bucket_date, dau, wau, mau. Backs the daily DAU/WAU/MAU line chart on the admin analytics page.

nodes.title: v_analytics_bounce_distribution_today
nodes.description: Postgres view: histogram of users by current bounce score (six buckets: 0, 1-10, 11-25, 26-50, 51-100, 100+) plus three summary stats denormalized onto every row — median_score, pct_maintaining (% of users whose current bounce >= bounce 7 days ago, reconstructed from karma_events), avg_active_days_per_week (avg distinct active days in the last 7 days across MAU). Always emits all six bucket rows, even when empty.

nodes.title: v_analytics_domain_share_weekly
nodes.description: Postgres view: one row per (ISO week, domain). Columns: bucket_week, domain_id, domain_slug, domain_name, domain_label, domain_level, pebbles_in_domain, total_pebbles, share_pct. Source: pebble_domains many-to-many, so a pebble can be linked to multiple domains and shares may exceed 100%. domain_level is derived from the seeded Maslow slug order (zoe, asphaleia, philia, time, eudaimonia).

nodes.title: v_analytics_emotion_share_weekly
nodes.description: Postgres view: one row per (ISO week, emotion). Columns: bucket_week, emotion_id, emotion_slug, emotion_name, color, pebbles_with_emotion, total_pebbles, share_pct. Source: pebbles.emotion_id (NOT NULL FK), so each pebble counts toward exactly one emotion and share_pct sums to 100% per week.

nodes.title: v_analytics_kpi_daily
nodes.description: Postgres view: one row per calendar day from the earliest pebble's created_at to today. Columns: bucket_date, total_users, dau, pebbles_today, wau, mau, dau_mau_pct. Aggregates auth.users and public.pebbles. Plain (non-materialized) view; will swap to MV when query times warrant.

nodes.title: v_analytics_pebble_enrichment_daily
nodes.description: Daily rollup of how enriched pebbles are: the share carrying a picture, a collection, a thought, a soul or an intensity. Revoked from public/anon/authenticated.

nodes.title: v_analytics_pebble_volume_daily
nodes.description: Daily rollup of pebble volume: pebbles recorded per day with the counts carrying a picture, a collection or a custom glyph, plus distinct active users. Revoked from public/anon/authenticated.

nodes.title: v_analytics_quality_signals_today
nodes.description: Postgres view: 8 rows describing today's habit-health indicators for the admin Quality signals table. Each row has indicator_order, indicator_key, indicator_label, unit, value (current period), previous_value (matching prior period), and available (false for the four indicators whose source data isn't captured yet — median session duration, sessions/WAU, % revisits to past pebbles, friction events/session). Phase A computes pebbles/WAU and D1 / D7 / D30 retention from public.pebbles + auth.users; the other four rows return null until sessions, pebble_views, and a normalized analytics_events table land in Phases B and C of issue #346.

nodes.title: v_analytics_retention_cohorts_weekly
nodes.description: Postgres view: one row per (cohort_week, week_offset). Cohort = users grouped by signup week (Mon–Sun, UTC) from auth.users.created_at. Columns: cohort_week, week_offset, cohort_size, active_users, retention_pct. retention_pct = % of cohort users who created >=1 pebble in that week_offset.

nodes.title: v_analytics_user_averages_weekly
nodes.description: Weekly per-user averages — what a typical active user records in a week, as opposed to the whole base's totals. Revoked from public/anon/authenticated.

nodes.title: v_domains_with_glyph
nodes.description: Postgres view (security_invoker): one row per domain — id, slug, name, label, default_glyph_id — left-joined to its glyph's strokes + view_box. Domain glyphs are system-owned (NULL user_id) so they read under the widened glyphs SELECT policy. Web reads this via useDomainGlyphs to render each domain's glyph beside its name; also available to iOS.

nodes.title: v_glyph_market
nodes.description: security_invoker view joining approved *and listed* glyph_submissions to their glyphs, carrying the listing price plus per-caller `owned` and `favourited` flags. The single read behind the market/Commu tab on all three surfaces, and the source of the web provider's entitled-glyph set (owned = true).

nodes.title: v_logs_with_counts
nodes.description: View over public.logs adding reaction_count. All four Lab feeds read it (announcements, changelog with released_at DESC NULLS LAST, initiatives, backlog by upvotes). Mobile clients decode rows lossily: a row with an unknown platform/species/status (incl. the project/infra platform values) is dropped whole — a deliberate cross-surface decision (M44 design D1).

nodes.title: wallet_balances
nodes.description: Postgres table: per-user spendable karma balance snapshot. Columns: user_id (PK, FK auth.users), balance (int, default 0; may go transiently negative on earn-side clawbacks — no non-negative CHECK, the overdraw guard lives in spend_karma), updated_at. Maintained atomically by trigger karma_events_apply_to_wallet on every karma_events insert (credit and withdraw). RLS: users read their own row; writes only via the trigger (security definer). Backfilled at migration time from sum(karma_events.delta) per user.

nodes.title: Back-office
nodes.description: The admin operator's journey through the Pebbles back-office (apps/admin, port 3001). Sign in with email + password, pass the requireAdmin() gate (no session redirects to the login page, a non-admin account redirects to the 403 page), then work in one of four sections: Insights, Pebblestore, Reference, Logs. The four sections are the sidebar's own groups.

nodes.description: The invite-only path to a mutual connection: open your invite, share the link or QR, and the person who opens it sees who is inviting and taps to connect. Accepting is the mutual consent — there is no request queue and no directory to search.

nodes.title: Achievement Unlock Moment
nodes.description: The unlock celebration: one card per badge that just unlocked, chained in catalog order and tapped through, showing the badge title, its copy and the karma that badge actually granted (as reported by the check, never the catalog's current value). Fires only from the mutation paths — creating a pebble, a soul, a collection, a mark — because the screen-open call on the Achievements grid is the retroactive grant and can return a veteran's whole history at once. Dismissal is never blocking: leaving skips the rest of the queue.

platformNotes.web: `AchievementMomentHost` mounted once in the root layout as a dialog; `fireAchievementCheck` pushes into it through a module-level emitter. The last card offers a `View achievements` button that navigates to /achievements.
